title: The Drowned Salt Again
premise: Quentin Kavanagh has spent his life as the invisible youngest of the Saltwright Guild, guiding smugglers through the Thornfell passes while hiding the tide-gift that lets him read water in stone and blood. When the crown's witch-hunt reaches the mountains, Quentin learns the king himself is bound to a drowned thing wearing his face, and that the guild's founding oath—sworn generations ago to protect the realm's last free waters—is the only magic that can unbind him. Betrayed by the guildmaster who raised him and hunted by his own brother-in-arms, Quentin must choose between loyalty to the dying guild and the truth of what it was built to hide. In the end, he breaks the oath, drowns the thing beneath Thornfell's salt lake, and inherits not the guild but the burden it was always meant to carry.
about_author: P. M. Iversen is a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping coastal caves before turning to fiction. They write from a house built on an old smuggler's route, where the sea is close enough to hear on quiet nights.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. He guides a smuggler caravan through the Thornfell passes while concealing his tide-gift, until royal hunters arrive bearing a proclamation: all gifted persons must surrender for 'culling.' The guildmaster, Odile, orders silence and secrecy, but Quentin glimpses her speaking privately with the hunters' captain. The emotional beat is dread—the safe world of belonging cracking open, and the first suspicion that the guild itself may have sold them out.

chapters.title: What the Oath Keeps
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, with interludes from Odile's old journal. Fleeing into the deep tunnels, Quentin discovers the guild's founding vault: records proving the first Saltwrights bound a drowned entity beneath the salt lake—and that every guildmaster since has fed it small truths to keep it sleeping. His closest friend, Bren, denounces him to save the guild. The beat is betrayal and revelation: loyalty and truth pull apart, and Quentin realizes invisibility was always the guild's design for him.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Captured and brought before the king, Quentin recognizes the drowned thing's signature in the water of the king's own body—it has worn the crown for thirty years, and the hunt for the gifted is its harvest. Odile arrives, confessing she bargained with it to spare the guild, and dies buying Quentin time to escape. The climax ignites: Quentin races back to Thornfell as the moon nears its thirteenth turn, choosing truth over every loyalty he had left.

chapters.title: Salt Remembers
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, joined at last by Bren, who returns seeking forgiveness. At the salt lake, Quentin speaks the unbinding—not the guild's oath of concealment, but the older words beneath it—and drags the drowned thing out of the king and into the open water, drowning it fully at moonrise. The king wakes diminished; the guild dissolves. The resolution is bittersweet inheritance: Quentin becomes keeper of the lake alone, no longer invisible, finally belonging to something true.
